// GetCveContentTypes return CveContentTypes
func GetCveContentTypes(family string) []CveContentType {
	if family == "trivy" {
		return []CveContentType{Trivy, TrivyDebian, TrivyUbuntu, TrivyNVD, TrivyRedHat, TrivyGHSA, TrivyOracleOVAL, TrivyAlpine}
	}

	// WpScan is WordPress
	WpScan CveContentType = "wpscan"

	// Trivy is Trivy
	Trivy           CveContentType = "trivy"
	TrivyDebian     CveContentType = "trivy:debian"
	TrivyUbuntu     CveContentType = "trivy:ubuntu"
	TrivyNVD        CveContentType = "trivy:nvd"
	TrivyRedHat     CveContentType = "trivy:redhat"

	TrivyOracleOVAL CveContentType = "trivy:oracle-oval"
	TrivyAlpine     CveContentType = "trivy:alpine"

	GitHub CveContentType = "github"

	// Unknown is Unknown
	Unknown CveContentType = "unknown"
)

item.text:
Implemented source-specific Trivy CVE content across conversion, library detection, model aggregation, and TUI references. Each source record preserves its vendor severity and CVSS metrics; the converter also keeps publication and modification dates when Trivy provides them.

Verified with `go test ./contrib/trivy/pkg ./models ./detector ./tui` and `git diff --check`.

The Trivy library database vulnerability record used by `detector/library.go` does not contain publication or modification dates, so that path cannot populate those fields.
